title: Pairs-DL: Deep learning spread forecasting for H155/H160
flagged_reason: HIGH RISK: prerequisite H160 not yet tested; H155 Kalman pairs already NOT CONFIRMED; deep learning on unvalidated signal. Requires Kevin review before queuing.
summary: Replace the threshold-based z-score entry in ETF pairs (H155, H160) with a GRU/LSTM spread forecast. Financial Analysis journal 2024 paper reports deep learning models for spread prediction outperform traditional z-score approaches in high-frequency context. VAR+GRU hybrid captures fat-tail dynamics that kill simple z-score strategies.

source.paper: Price spread prediction in high-frequency pairs trading using deep learning architectures
source.paper2: Combined Effects of Fat-Tail and Spread Forecasting on Pairs Trading: A Hybrid Model Based on Integrating VAR With GRU Models
source.key_finding: VAR+GRU hybrid with fat-tail modeling outperforms z-score baseline across multiple ETF pairs

implementation.architecture: VAR (vector autoregression) for covariance structure + GRU for nonlinear spread dynamics
implementation.target: spread direction in next N bars (classification) or spread level (regression)
implementation.prerequisite: H160 factor-residualized pairs must be identified first (rolling OLS vs SPY + sector ETF)

expected_improvement: Better entry timing — enter when model predicts reversion, not just when z > 2. Reduces false positives (pairs that gap but don't revert).
risks: High complexity — easy to overfit on small ETF pair universe
Requires daily retraining or at minimum monthly update
H155 (Kalman pairs) already NOT CONFIRMED — deep learning on a broken signal may not help
Better to nail H160 factor residualization first, then layer on ML
recommendation: Queue after H160 is confirmed. Do not apply before H160 PARTIAL or better verdict.
